subject.title: Feature Request: Cross-platform migration tool (migrate export/import)

question: Should OpenClaw core own automated same-product archive export/import, and if so should it live under `migrate export/import` or the backup/restore command family?
rationale: The answer determines CLI namespace, archive trust policy, secret/session portability, destructive write behavior, and whether overlapping backup/plugin work should proceed in core.

options.title: Define a minimal native import contract
options.body: Approve a preview-first core export/import or backup-restore lifecycle with canonical target validation, explicit secret/session policy, rollback/conflict handling, and security-focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Improve backup plus manual restore
options.body: Keep automated restore out of core for now and improve backup output, platform targeting, verification, and public migration docs so users can migrate safely with fewer manual guesses.

options.title: Route optional sync to plugins
options.body: Keep core limited to archive verification and missing APIs while ClawHub or plugin packages own cloud sync, scheduled backups, and ecosystem-specific workflows.

recommendation.title: Define a minimal native import contract
recommendation.body: Approve a preview-first core export/import or backup-restore lifecycle with canonical target validation, explicit secret/session policy, rollback/conflict handling, and security-focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice centers on CLI ownership and backup/import safety semantics, where gumadeiras is the strongest observed routing candidate from maintainer areas and backup path history.
